scenarios.title: Family Calls: {J} Asked for Help
text: His mother doesn't ask directly. She never does. She just mentions that an uncle's warung is failing, and then talks about the weather for ten minutes. {J} understands exactly what is being asked.
His sister calls in tears: the university fees are due on Friday and their father's business had a bad month. She hasn't asked for anything. She doesn't need to.
scenarios.prompt: Your family needs about {amount}. What do you do?

choices.label: Send it all
choices.text: The money goes that night. His mother sends a voice note that is mostly crying and a little bit laughing.

choices.label: Monthly support
choices.desc: Set up a regular transfer instead.
choices.text: {J} sets up a monthly transfer. It feels like being an adult in a way that scoring never has.

choices.label: Say no
choices.text: The silence in the family group chat for the next few days is loud.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Father Is in Hospital
scenarios.text: The call comes at 5am. His father collapsed at work. Heart problems. He's stable, the doctors say, but needs an operation, and the good hospital in the city costs {cost}.

choices.label: Pay for the best care and fly home
choices.hint: The right thing. The club should understand.
choices.text: {J} pays for the operation and sits by the bed for five days. His father squeezes his hand and says only, “Go back. Play well.” The club sends flowers.

choices.label: Pay, stay with the team
choices.desc: Your father would want you to play.
choices.hint: Your family may not see it that way.
choices.text: {J} pays for everything and stays. He plays on Saturday and points to the sky after a good tackle. His mother doesn't call for three days.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Father Walks Into the Stadium
scenarios.text: Three months after the operation, {J}'s father sits in the stand for the first time since he got sick. Slower, thinner, wearing a club scarf his wife had to wrap twice. When {J} warms up, he waves. {J} has to look away for a second.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Younger Brother Wants to Be a Footballer
scenarios.text: His fifteen-year-old brother calls: an academy has offered him a trial. He's good, but not as good as {J} was. Their mother wants {J} to decide whether he should go.

choices.label: Support him all the way
choices.text: {J} pays {cost} for boots and a summer programme. His brother sends him a video of every training session.

choices.label: Tell him the truth
choices.text: {J} tells his brother how few make it. His brother goes quiet. Their mother says he was too harsh.

scenarios.title: News From {J}'s Brother's Trial
scenarios.text: The academy has made a decision about {J}'s younger brother.

out.text: He's in! A scholarship at the academy. He screams down the phone. {J} screams back.
Released. He's trying not to cry. {J} tells him about all the times he nearly gave up. They talk for two hours.

scenarios.title: {J} Can Buy His Parents a House
scenarios.text: For the first time, {J} has enough savings to buy his parents a proper house. They've lived in the same small rented place for twenty years. His mother says they don't need it. She has been looking at house listings on her phone.

choices.label: Buy it
choices.desc: The moment you've dreamed of since you were nine.
choices.text: {J} hands his parents the keys on a Sunday afternoon. His father walks around every room twice without speaking. His mother cries in the kitchen. It's the best day of {J}'s life.

choices.label: Wait a few years
choices.text: {J} decides to wait until his finances are safer. His mother says she understands, and means it.

scenarios.title: Back in {J}'s Hometown
scenarios.text: Off-season. {J} goes home. The streets feel smaller. Old friends work in shops and drive ojek. Kids follow him everywhere. Everyone wants something: a photo, an autograph, a loan, advice.
scenarios.prompt: How do you spend your time at home?

choices.label: Free football clinic for kids
choices.desc: Give back to where it started.
choices.text: Two hundred kids on a dusty pitch, {J} in the middle of it all. The local paper runs it on the front page.

choices.label: Rest with family
choices.text: Two weeks of his mother's cooking and his father's terrible jokes. He goes back heavier and happier.

choices.label: Catch up with old friends
choices.hint: Not all old friendships survive fame.

out.text: The old crew treats him exactly the same as always. It's the most normal he's felt in a year.
An old friend asks for a large loan and won't take no for an answer. Things get awkward.

scenarios.title: Cousin's Wedding on Match Day
scenarios.text: His favourite cousin is getting married. The wedding is on the same day as a league match. The family expects {J} to be there. The club expects him on the pitch.
scenarios.prompt: Ask for permission to miss the match?

choices.label: Ask the club
choices.hint: The manager might say no — or remember.

out.text: {M} grudgingly agrees. {J} dances at the wedding, and his cousin gives a speech about him. Worth it.
{M} says no. {J} sends a video message. His aunt is still angry about it at the next family gathering.

choices.label: Play the match
choices.desc: Send a gift and a video.
choices.text: {J} plays, then joins the reception by video call. The bride holds the phone up to show him the dancing.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Grandmother Passes Away
scenarios.text: His grandmother, who walked him to every training session when he was small, who kept every newspaper clipping in a shoebox under her bed, has passed away. The funeral is in two days, a long way from here.
scenarios.prompt: The club will let you go.

choices.label: Go to the funeral
choices.text: {J} carries her coffin with his father and uncles. Afterwards his aunt gives him the shoebox. It's full of him.

choices.label: Play in her honour
choices.text: {J} plays with a black armband and points to the sky. His aunt says it's what grandma would have wanted. Not everyone agrees.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Parents Visit Him Abroad
scenarios.text: His parents arrive for a week: first time on a plane, first time abroad. His mother has packed sambal, krupuk and dried fish in a suitcase that set off two alarms at customs. His father wears a new shirt bought for the trip.
scenarios.prompt: How do you spend the week?

choices.label: Show them everything
choices.text: {J} shows them the city, the stadium, the training ground. His father shakes {M}'s hand for a full minute.

choices.label: Quiet week at home
choices.text: A week of his mother cooking in his tiny kitchen. The apartment smells like home for the first time.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Mother Watches Him Play Live for the First Time
scenarios.text: His mother has watched every match on a phone screen. She has never been to a stadium. This weekend, {J} has paid for her flight and a seat behind the dugout. She's terrified of the crowd.

scenarios.title: Family Asks: When Will {J} Get Married?
scenarios.text: At every family gathering, every phone call, the same question. Aunts suggest daughters of friends. His mother sends photos “just to look”.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.text: The aunts laugh too. The photos keep coming.

choices.label: Agree to meet someone
choices.hint: Could be lovely. Could be awkward.

out.text: The dinner is surprisingly lovely. {F} is smart, funny, and doesn't care about football.
The dinner is painfully awkward. Both mothers are disappointed.

scenarios.title: Uncle's Business Proposal
scenarios.text: An uncle has a business proposal: a fleet of minibuses, a guaranteed route, “everyone in the family is in”. He needs {cost} from {J}.

choices.label: Invest
choices.hint: Could be fine. Could ruin Christmas forever.

out.text: The minibuses run. Profits are small, but real. Uncle is very proud.
Six months later, the minibuses are sold and nobody knows where the money went. Family gatherings are tense.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.text: {J} gives a small gift instead. The uncle is offended for a year, then forgets.

scenarios.title: The Minibus Business Pays Out
scenarios.text: Twenty months after {J} invested, his uncle shows up at the family house with an envelope and a big grin. The minibuses made money.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Father Has Notes
scenarios.text: His father calls after every match with a list of mistakes. Tonight the list is long. “Why didn't you pass? Why didn't you run back?” He means well. It doesn't feel like it.

choices.label: Listen patiently
choices.text: {J} listens to all fourteen points. Some are even right.

out.text: His father goes quiet, then laughs. “Okay. From now on, I only say good things.” He doesn't manage it, but he tries.
His father hangs up. Their next three calls are short.

scenarios.title: Floods Hit {J}'s Home Village
scenarios.text: The rainy season brings floods to {J}'s home village. His parents' house has water up to the windows. They're staying at a school hall with two hundred other families.

choices.label: Fund relief for the whole village
choices.text: {J} pays for food parcels, clean water and repairs for the whole village. His name is painted on the new school wall.

choices.label: Help your family
choices.text: {J} pays {small} for his parents' repairs. They move back in within a month.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Mother's Birthday
scenarios.text: It's his mother's birthday. She says she doesn't want anything. She says that every year.

choices.label: Fly home for one day
choices.text: {J} knocks on the door at 7pm with a cake. His mother screams so loudly the neighbours come running.

choices.label: Send a big gift
choices.hint: She'll wear them to every wedding.
choices.text: Gold earrings worth {cost}. She wears them to every family event for the next ten years.

choices.label: A long video call
choices.hint: She just wants to hear from you.
choices.text: Two hours on video. She tells him about every neighbour. He listens to all of it.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Family Gets Unwanted Attention
scenarios.text: Fans have started visiting his parents' house. Some bring gifts. Some just stand outside taking photos. Yesterday someone climbed the fence.

choices.label: Hire security for the house
choices.text: {J} hires a security guard for {cost}. His mother feeds the guard so much he gains five kilos.

choices.label: Post a polite request
choices.text: The post works, mostly. The visits drop off.

scenarios.title: Sister's Wedding: Who Pays?
scenarios.text: His sister is getting married. The family expects {J}, the famous one, to help pay for a big wedding: five hundred guests, a band, a full buffet. The total is {cost}.

choices.label: Pay for everything
choices.text: {J} pays for everything. His sister's wedding is the talk of the town for a year.

choices.label: Pay half
choices.text: {J} pays half. Some relatives grumble that the famous brother could do more.

scenarios.title: Video Call at Sahur
scenarios.text: 3:30am. His mother calls during sahur, as she does every day of Ramadan, to make sure he's eating. She can see the empty fridge behind him on the video. She is not impressed.

scenarios.title: Lebaran: Will {J} Go Home for Eid?
scenarios.text: Idul Fitri is coming. All of Indonesia is going home: mudik, the great journey back to the kampung. His family is counting on him for the first day of Lebaran. The club has a match two days later.

choices.label: Go home for the first day
choices.text: {J} kneels before his parents and asks for forgiveness for the year's mistakes, as every Indonesian child does. His father puts a hand on his head. Then ketupat, opor ayam, and fifty relatives asking for photos.

choices.label: Stay with the club
choices.desc: Video call, send THR money home.
choices.hint: Your mother will cry on the call.
choices.text: {J} sends {thr} as THR for the whole family and joins the gathering by video. His mother cries. His little cousins ask why he's in a box.

scenarios.title: {J}'s First Coach Is Sick
scenarios.text: News from home: the coach who found {J} at nine years old, who drove him to tournaments in his own car, who bought his first proper boots, is sick and can't afford treatment.

choices.label: Pay for his treatment
choices.text: {J} pays and visits. The old man cries and tells the nurses: “I found him. Me.”

choices.label: Send a message
choices.text: A heartfelt message. The coach shows it to everyone in the ward.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Brother Is in Trouble
scenarios.text: His younger brother has fallen in with the wrong crowd at home: debts, gambling, a fight at a night market. His mother calls in a panic. Someone is threatening him.

choices.label: Pay the debt and bring him to live with you
choices.text: {J} pays {cost} and moves his brother into his spare room. It's hard. It's also the best thing for both of them.

out.text: The debt is paid and his brother is scared straight. For now.
Three months later, a new debt. Bigger.

choices.label: Refuse to pay
choices.text: {J} refuses. His mother doesn't speak to him for a month. His brother eventually sorts it out himself, barely.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Parents on National TV
scenarios.text: A national TV station visits {J}'s parents for a feature on his career. His father wears a suit for the first time since his wedding. His mother shows the shoebox of newspaper clippings to the camera.

scenarios.title: A Message From {J}'s Old Teacher
scenarios.text: His primary school teacher, the one who told him he'd never amount to anything because he only cared about football, sends a message: “I was wrong about you. My whole class watches your matches now.”

scenarios.title: Every Relative Has a Request
scenarios.text: At the family gathering, the requests come one after another: a cousin wants a phone, an aunt wants help with rent, a distant relative wants him to invest in a durian farm.

choices.label: Help everyone a little
choices.text: {J} spends {cost} on small gifts and favours. Everyone is happy. The requests will be back next year.

choices.label: Set clear boundaries
choices.text: {J} explains he can only support his parents and siblings. A few relatives call him arrogant. His father defends him.

scenarios.title: Little Cousin's First Match in the Stadium
scenarios.text: {J} gets tickets for his little cousin, eight years old, to watch his first ever live match. The boy wears {J}'s shirt down to his knees.

scenarios.title: {J} Can Let His Father Retire
scenarios.text: His father has worked six days a week for thirty-one years. With {cost}, {J} could set up a fund so he never has to work again.

choices.label: Do it
choices.text: His father argues for twenty minutes, then says yes. The next morning, for the first time in thirty-one years, he sleeps in. He calls {J} at 10am to complain he doesn't know what to do with himself.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.text: {J} waits. His father wouldn't have accepted yet anyway.

scenarios.title: Hometown Club Asks for Help
scenarios.text: The amateur club in {J}'s hometown, where he played as a boy, is about to fold. They need money for pitch rental and kit. The chairman, an old man who used to referee his games, writes a letter by hand.

choices.label: Fund the club for five years
choices.text: The club is saved. They rename the youth team after him. Forty kids play there every weekend.

choices.label: Donate kit
choices.text: New kits for every age group. The club survives another season.

scenarios.title: A Teammate's Child Is Sick
scenarios.text: {T}'s young daughter is seriously ill. He's been coming to training with red eyes and leaving immediately after. The squad wants to do something.

choices.label: Organise a squad fund
choices.text: The squad raises enough to cover the treatment. {T} breaks down in the dressing room. Nobody says anything. Everyone hugs him.

choices.label: Visit the hospital
choices.text: {J} visits with a giant teddy bear. The little girl names it after him.

scenarios.title: Distance Grows Between {J} and His Family
scenarios.text: The calls have become shorter. The family group chat is quiet when he posts. His mother's messages are polite. Something has broken, slowly, and nobody has said it out loud.

out.text: Three hours around the kitchen table. Tears, some shouting, then laughter. It's better.
The talk goes badly. Old resentments come out. It will take time.

choices.label: Write a long letter
choices.desc: Say what you can't say out loud.
choices.text: {J} writes four pages by hand. His mother keeps it in her handbag.

scenarios.title: Family Banner in the Stands
scenarios.text: His whole family — parents, siblings, cousins, an elderly aunt in a wheelchair — arrive at the stadium with a homemade banner: “{J}, OUR PRIDE”. The TV cameras find it in the first minute.

scenarios.title: {J} Becomes an Uncle
scenarios.text: His older sister has given birth to a baby boy. The first photo arrives at 4am: tiny, wrinkled, furious. His sister writes: “He's going to be a footballer like his uncle.”

choices.label: A tiny club kit with your name
choices.text: The photo of the baby in a tiny shirt with {J} on the back is the most liked thing he's ever posted.

choices.label: A savings account
choices.text: {J} opens a savings account for his nephew with {cost}. His sister cries.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Mother Wants Him to Finish His Studies
scenarios.text: {J} left school at sixteen for football. His mother has never stopped mentioning it. She's found an online university programme designed for athletes.

choices.label: Enrol
choices.hint: Tired, but your mother will be thrilled.
choices.text: {J} enrols in a sports management degree. He's tired. His mother tells everyone at the market.

choices.label: Not now
choices.text: “After my career, Ma.” She sighs. She'll ask again.

scenarios.title: {J} Graduates
scenarios.text: After years of studying at night, {J} completes his degree. His mother attends the ceremony in her best clothes and cries louder than when he signed his first contract.
